📊 Intro Statistics Formulas

This tutor practices 60 core statistics formulas that students often need to recognize quickly in an introductory course.

  • What you will do: Each card shows a formula or symbolic expression, and you type a short identifying label such as the name of the statistic, test, or distribution.
  • Timing: Study screens last about 16 seconds, drill screens about 8 seconds, review screens about 5 seconds, and correct confirmations last about 0.75 seconds.
  • How it works: Immediate feedback helps you separate visually similar formulas before they blur together, especially when sample and population notation differ by only one symbol.
  • Why it helps: Adaptive scheduling returns shaky formulas sooner and spaces familiar ones farther apart for stronger exam and homework fluency.

Read each expression carefully, watch for notation such as mu, sigma, x-bar, and s, then begin when you are ready.

learningsession.calculateProbability: p.y = -0.45 + .73* pFunc.logitdec( p.overallOutcomeHistory.slice( Math.max(p.overallOutcomeHistory.length-60,  0),   p.overallOutcomeHistory.length),  .95)+ .52* Math.log(1+p.stimSuccessCount) + 2.17 * pFunc.recency(p.stimSecsSinceLastShown,  .30) ; p.probability = 1.0 / (1.0 + Math.exp(-p.y));  return p

Great work!

You've completed your statistics formula practice session. The adaptive system has been tracking your progress and will continue to optimize your learning on future sessions.

Common formulas to remember:

  • Descriptive: Mean, variance, and standard deviation form the foundation
  • Inference: Standard error connects samples to populations
  • Testing: t-tests and z-tests help make decisions from data
  • Relationships: Correlation and regression reveal patterns

Continue practicing to build fluency with these essential statistical tools!
